objective: Cross the sea east to Autumn Wood: Tsumugi has found the Court's couriers
title: Ink in the Maples
summary: The Watch's records burned in the night. The couriers who burned them are still on the road, and one of them keeps a ledger of names.

say: Don't ask. I know what you're going to ask. The Watch's archive burned last night, every shelf, and I was asleep forty paces away.

lines: Everything but one page, which was in my boot. It's the only thing I keep in my boot, so naturally they missed it.
The Court has no army. It has couriers, and a ledger. Whoever is written in the Ledger is forgotten: not dead, just not remembered.
By everyone. By their mothers. That's what 'hollow' means, {name}. The Court is made of people who were written out, and who stayed.
The couriers carry the pages to the Ink-Hand, who writes. They're on the maple road now. Stop them before the rain does what the fire didn't.

beats.text: Stop the couriers on the maple road

say: Oh dear. You've scattered my couriers. They were very good couriers.
I am Sumi. I keep the Ledger. I'm sorry about this, truly. It is such a quiet job, and it does so poorly with company.
She's the one who wrote my sister out of my own house.
Was she? There are so many. I am sorry, I cannot recall her name.

beats.taunt: Hold still. It stings less if you hold still.

phases.say: Wet ink spreads. That is rather the point.

lines: ...You are stubborn. The Ledger said you would be, and I did not believe the Ledger.
Where is the Court's Ledger kept?
Under the dam. Where the water keeps it, and the Ash Blade keeps the road to it. Ask him, if he lets you ask.
He took the Court's coin to rebuild a shrine. You must not think ill of him. Everyone has a price. His was kind.
She hid behind that quiet voice, and she still wrote my sister out. I do not forgive her.
But I heard what she said about the dam. Go. I will hold the road.
